text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps other developers work with it. Good naming conventions make a big difference: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Keep functions small and focused on one task, because short functions are easier to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, since bugs are simpler to find and changes are safer to make. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces problems for the whole team.
